parts.text: Overview

blocks.text: This report is published by RWA Foundation using data from DefiLlama's RWA perpetuals dataset. It covers onchain perpetual futures referencing real-world assets, ranked by venue, asset class, reference-asset group and individual market. All figures are 30-day trailing, with month-over-month changes measured against the preceding 30 days.

blocks.text: Across DefiLlama's tracked RWA perp dataset, 1,086 active markets across 19 venues generated $117.31B in 30-day volume, down 10.1%, while average daily open interest rose 6.0% to $5.15B. Trade.xyz remains the largest venue, but its share of volume fell from 73.2% to 46.7%, and on September 23rd, Variational out-traded it for the first time.

blocks.text: The decline sits almost entirely in single stocks, as the memory and semiconductor trade that dominated last month unwound. Much of the offsetting growth came from markets listed during the month.

parts.text: Venue Landscape

blocks.text: Nineteen venues now carry tracked RWA perp volume, up from sixteen, and the distribution is less top-heavy than a month ago. Trade.xyz, a Hyperliquid HIP-3 deployer, generated $54.77B, down 42.6%, yet still carries roughly 73% of open interest. Seven memory and semiconductor markets account for about two-thirds of its decline.

blocks.text: @Variational_io is now a clear second at $26.88B (22.9%), up from $5.86B, with its newly listed Nasdaq-100 market alone accounting for $14.19B. On September 23 and 24 it out-traded Trade.xyz, the first days it has done so since its history in the dataset begins in May. gmtrade ranks third at $13.77B (11.7%), up 28.9%.

blocks.text: Where Volume Moved

parts.text: Where Volume Moved

blocks.text: Public equities lost $32.8B of volume over the month, while every other reference-asset group combined added a net $19.6B, most of it from newly listed markets.

parts.text: Public equities lost $32.8B of volume over the month, while every other reference-asset group combined added a net $19.6B, most of it from newly listed markets.

blocks.text: Equity Indices gained $14.1B (81.5%), but Variational's new Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500 markets generated $18.1B between them. Precious Metals rose $3.9B on a similar pattern, driven by Variational's new gold and silver contracts. Oil, up $3.2B (27.7%), is the one group where growth was broad-based. AI & Compute Infrastructure, which last month pointed to an emerging niche, fell 64.5% to $1.88B.

blocks.text: Open interest offers a steadier read. It rose 12.8% in precious metals and 11.3% in oil, while equity indices saw a burst of trading with open interest down 2.6%.

blocks.text: Stock-perps remain the largest asset class at $38.54B (32.9% share), down from 54.6%, with commodity-perps a close second at $34.52B (29.4%), up 25.0%. Stock-perp listings grew to 790 markets, yet average volume per stock market fell from $133.4M to $50.4M.

parts.text: Stock-perps remain the largest asset class at $38.54B (32.9% share), down from 54.6%, with commodity-perps a close second at $34.52B (29.4%), up 25.0%. Stock-perp listings grew to 790 markets, yet average volume per stock market fell from $133.4M to $50.4M.

blocks.text: Index products sit under two DefiLlama tags, equity-index-perp and equity-perp, split by how each venue's markets were recorded rather than by product. Together they generated $30.67B (26.1%), up 85%. Forex-perps grew 27.9% to $8.92B, while etf-perps fell 47.3% to $4.14B. Private-equity, bond and crypto-index perps remain nascent at 0.4% of volume.

blocks.text: The largest market this month, Variational's Nasdaq-100 perp, did not exist a month ago and generated $14.19B, more than twice any other. Trade.xyz's WTI crude oil market ranks second at $6.89B, up 30%.

blocks.text: The memory-chip names that led last month have fallen sharply. SK hynix drops from first to third, Sandisk from second to ninth, and Micron out of the top ten. Across seven memory and semiconductor markets on Trade.xyz, volume fell 62.8%, and their share of the venue's volume fell from 45.7% to 29.6%.

blocks.text: Closing Statement

parts.text: Closing Statement

blocks.text: The RWA perpetuals market remains new and concentrated, but less so than a month ago. The memory and semiconductor exposure that drove last month's volume has unwound, and the activity replacing it came largely from new listings rather than deeper trading in established markets.

parts.text: The RWA perpetuals market remains new and concentrated, but less so than a month ago. The memory and semiconductor exposure that drove last month's volume has unwound, and the activity replacing it came largely from new listings rather than deeper trading in established markets.

blocks.text: Positions tell a steadier story. Open interest rose 6.0%, and Trade.xyz, despite losing more than a third of its volume share, still holds nearly three-quarters of it. Whether Variational's new markets retain their volume beyond launch is the central question for next month.
